categories.name: Accuracy
categories.reason: Every number recomputed from official WNBA.com play-by-play and matched to the box score for all players in all 7 games; records attributed to the Valkyries release; quotes from AP and The Athletic as published on WNBA.com.

categories.name: Information gain
categories.reason: First public quarter-by-quarter and half-by-half ledger of Williams' 137 Finals points, plus the series-wide second-half leaderboard (51 fourth-quarter points, 22 more than anyone).

categories.name: Effort
categories.reason: Parsed seven official play-by-play logs (2,700+ events), cross-checked every player total, built two CSVs and a chart.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: Outlets reported the 28-point half; none mapped when she scored across the series or contrasted her split with Reese's.

categories.name: Experience
categories.reason: Data-driven desk work; no first-hand reporting from Chase Center.

categories.name: Layout
categories.reason: Key finding and data table sit directly under the intro with methods, sources and data-through date; news context below.

categories.name: Transparency
categories.reason: Methods, linked per-game sources, CC0 downloads and the standard How this story was made note.

categories.name: Writing craft
categories.reason: Sentence-case result-first headline, short sentences, no filler, no em dashes.

categories.name: People-first
categories.reason: Answers what fans and reporters search for (Finals MVP stats) with something new and reusable.

categories.name: Human voice
categories.reason: Plain, direct copy; real quotes carry the emotion instead of invented reactions.

info_gain: Williams scored 85 of 137 Finals points after halftime and 51 in fourth quarters; next best was Rhyne Howard with 29.
In Games 6 and 7 she scored 50 of her 56 points in the second half.
Angel Reese had the opposite split: 65 of her 103 points before halftime.
She made 23 of 24 second-half free throws and shot 34.6% after halftime vs 29.8% before.
